advisories.text: Rust projection turns not:{pattern} into not:{} on Common1/Common3/Identity3/Occupancy1 LogicalPath, which is unsatisfiable as schema. typify 0.8.0 ignores not (path-ok and path-dotdot both accepted by Rust; TS runtime rejects a/../b), so there is no current loss, but it would be uninhabited under a tool that honours not. Drop a not whose body becomes empty and guard it.

The Rust carrier collapses duplicate map keys last-wins (fp-duplicate-map-key accepted as {a:2}); duplicate struct fields refuse. The TS exact codec refuses both. Rust carriers must only receive bytes after exact admission. Roundtrip evidence is serde_json Value equality without preserve_order or arbitrary_precision: key-order-insensitive, not byte-level.

Over-acceptance by inert Rust carriers is confirmed and expected: pattern, propertyNames pattern, if/then, x-opensip-order and not are not enforced, and FieldPresence<Option<T>> on non-nullable optional members admits a present null (preserved on output). The TS runtime on original schemas rejects all of these. Typed carriers must remain post-admission only.

The requested command `rustfmt --edition2024` fails on rustfmt 1.9.0 (Unrecognized option: 'edition2024'); `rustfmt --edition 2024` reproduces output-b. The drift recipe must record the exact command and formatter version.

prepare.py schema_map traverses a fixed keyword set and silently passes others. The input inventory has no untraversed applicators, but the adapter should refuse keywords outside an allowlist matching the runtime known/annotation sets (schema.ts:16-17).
